title: ShaderProgram.reloadWithFragmentSource keeps the old source after a successful compile and the broken one after a failed one
description: ShaderProgram.reloadWithFragmentSource(src) (ShaderProgram.java ~470) stores the new fragment source, recompiles, and then, if the compile SUCCEEDED, puts the previous source back. So after a success the GPU runs the new shader while the program records the old source, and anything that recompiles from the stored source later (hot reload, a context rebuild) silently reverts it; after a failure the broken source stays stored, so the next recompile fails again. The condition looks inverted: restore the previous source when the compile fails. Check its callers (the code pane's line preview, ShaderCodePane / restoreOriginal at ~580) still behave after the fix. Found by UI-12.
definition-of-done:
1. After a successful reloadWithFragmentSource the stored fragment source is the new one; after a failed one it is the previous one and the previous program still runs.
2. The code pane's line preview and restore still work on line-canvas.
3. A test covers both branches (with a GL stand-in if needed).
testing-plan:
1. Unit test with a GL stand-in for success and failure.
2. ixdar-cli on line-canvas: click a code line, then the preview; screenshots under tmp/.
